task: share a file, folder, or photo album with specific people at the right permission level (Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, OneDrive, iCloud): pick the item, open the sharing dialog, add people or create a link, set the permission (viewer/commenter/editor; link scope), send the invite or copy the link, and verify who has access; complete when the shared state (the people list, or the created link with its permission) is on screen. Surface pinned: a cloud storage or photos service's share flow. Variants: file-transfer-service marketing, torrenting, IT-admin tenant sharing policies, and camera/photography content do not belong.

questions.check: Does the confirmation dialog show the correct recipients and permission level before it closes?
questions.say_example: The confirmation shows <name> as <editor> - not what was set up.

questions.question: Did the visual badge on the file icon update to show it is now shared?
questions.why: After sharing, the file or folder icon in the main storage view updates to include a 'shared' badge (like a small group of people), providing persistent visual proof of its state.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the persistent visual confirmation in the main file explorer that the item's state has successfully changed to shared.
questions.check: Did the file or folder icon update to show a 'shared' badge?
questions.say_example: The icon never picked up the shared badge - the share may not have gone through.

children.label: Manage or revoke the share
children.note: 9.1 to change a person's standing grant, 9.2 to change the token's; 9.3 ends it from the owner's side and 9.4 from the recipient's - both warn that content vanishes from other people's devices

questions.question: Should you adjust individual permissions or stop sharing the file entirely?
questions.why: The dialog provides options to change a specific user's access level via the three-dot menu or to revoke all access using the 'Stop Sharing' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the final say on whether to tweak individual access rights or completely lock down the file.
questions.verify_form: Check which lever the agent pulled - one person's level, or Stop Sharing, which pulls the file back from everyone at once.
questions.check: Did the agent adjust one person's access, or use 'Stop Sharing' to pull access from everyone at once?
questions.say_example: Changed one person's access, not the whole share

questions.question: Who do you want to add or remove from the Shared Library?
questions.why: The Shared Library settings display current participants and provide options to add new people or remove existing ones.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to review the participant list and make specific additions or removals.
questions.verify_form: Check the participant list after the agent touched it - who got added, who removed; every name on it holds full edit rights.
questions.check: Do the participants currently listed for the Shared Library match who was added or removed?
questions.say_example: <name> is still on the Shared Library list after being asked to remove them.

questions.question: Do you want to remove this participant or view their contact card?
questions.why: The screen displays a context menu for '[email]' with options to either show their contact card or remove them from the share list.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify the participant's identity or decide if their access should be revoked.
questions.verify_form: Check what the agent did in the participant's menu - a removal cuts that person's access on the spot.
questions.check: Did the agent remove the participant, or just view their contact card?
questions.say_example: Removed <name> from the share - their access ends now.

questions.question: Whose permission level do you need to modify?
questions.why: The 'Manage Access' pane lists multiple collaborators with varying current access levels, so you must select the correct individual to update.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct oversight of ensuring the correct collaborator's access rights are modified without accidentally altering someone else's permissions.
questions.verify_form: Check which person's row the agent changed in Manage Access; the wrong row re-permissions the wrong human.
questions.check: Does the row modified in Manage Access belong to the person actually intended?
questions.say_example: That row belongs to <a different person> than the one you meant to change.

questions.question: This link change affects everyone who has it, not just you. Still change it?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning that modifying the link setting will impact everyone who currently has access via that link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to evaluate how this permission change will disrupt or alter access for existing collaborators.
questions.verify_form: The change-it dialog warns the edit hits everyone using the link - check the new level was meant for all of them, not one person.
questions.check: Does the warning say this link-setting change affects everyone currently using that link, not just one person?
questions.say_example: Changing this link's setting affects everyone who has it, not just one person. Still change it?

questions.question: How do you modify the specific link granting access to this user?
questions.why: The access summary shows the person has access via a specific link rather than direct access, meaning you must adjust that link's settings to change their permissions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to audit exactly which link is granting access and manually fine-tune its specific permissions.
questions.check: Does the access summary show this person's access comes through a specific link rather than a direct grant?
questions.say_example: This person's access comes from a link, not a direct grant - adjusting the link changes it for them

questions.question: Do you want to permanently delete this file from the shared drive?
questions.why: The screen displayed a warning that the file would be deleted forever and could not be restored.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to prevent irreversible data loss if the agent permanently deletes a file without explicit permission.
questions.verify_form: The agent confirmed a delete-forever - check which file; there is no bin after this one.
questions.check: Does the warning say this file will be permanently deleted and cannot be restored?
questions.say_example: This deletes the file forever, for everyone it's shared with, with no way back. Still delete it?

questions.question: Are you sure you want to stop sharing and delete this document from everyone else's devices?
questions.why: The confirmation dialog explicitly warns that stopping the share will revoke access and delete the document from iCloud Drive on all collaborators' devices.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to evaluate whether the disruptive consequence of deleting the file from others' devices is truly intended before proceeding.
questions.verify_form: Stop Sharing removes the doc from every collaborator's devices - check that blast was intended before trusting the confirm.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say stopping sharing will remove the document from every collaborator's device?
questions.say_example: Stopping this share deletes the document from everyone's devices, not just yours. Still stop sharing?

questions.question: Do you want to remove yourself from this shared file?
questions.why: The Manage Shared File dialog shows a 'Remove Me' option next to your name that will delete the shared document from your drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might permanently remove your access to a shared document without your explicit confirmation.
questions.verify_form: Remove Me deletes the shared doc from your own devices - check the agent didn't cut your access while tidying up.
questions.check: Does 'Remove Me' delete the shared file from only the agent's own devices, or from everyone's?
questions.say_example: Remove Me only takes this off your own devices - everyone else keeps their access.
